To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Photosynthetic capacity and leaf-level stomatal conductance vary independently in soybean, and this variation contributes to differences in intrinsic WUE before and during mild water deficit.

1) the contribution of stomata to WUE(in) was the largest contributor to variation in WUE (intr) in soybean, and 2) the contribution of photosynthesis to WUE(in), was independent of the contribution of stomatas, and 3) photosynthetic capacity was not reduced by mild drought, and 4) the maximal rate of Rubiscocarboxylation was correlated with photosynthesis.
the contribution of photosynthesis and stomatal conductances to soybean intrinsic water use efficiency varies independently between genotypes and is not altered by mild drought.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of genetic factors that influence photosynthetic capacity, and the use of such information to enhance the efficiency of soybean production in the context of water scarcity.
the development of a new selection strategy for breeding water saving soybean genotypes with high photosynthesic capacities.
the development of a breeding program to produce water efficient soybeans with high yields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

genotypic differences in photosynthetic capacities and stomatal conductances are independent of each other and that these traits contribute to differences in intrinsic WUE in a non-interactive manner.
photosynthetic capacity is a more important factor than stomatal conductance for determining WUE(intr).
the contribution of photosynthesis and stomatal conductances to the variation in WUEintr is independent of each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the contribution of photosynthesis and stomatal conductances to intrinsic water use efficiency varied independently between 11 soybean lines and this pattern was interactive only with mild drought.
genotypic differences in the two components of WUE(intr), photosynthetic capacity, and stomatal conduct, are independent, and thus selection for both traits should be employed to maximize WUE(intr).

the contribution of photosynthesis and stomatal conductances to intrinsic water use efficiency (intrinsic WUE, the ratio of photosynthetic rate to stomatal conductances) varied independently between 11 soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.] genotypes and that this pattern was interactive between genotypes and mild drought.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the contribution of photosynthesis to WUE(intrs) and the contribution of stomata to WUE(intras) are independent of each other, and thus, the use of WUE(intras), while useful, is not a substitute for knowledge of both photosynthetic and stomatal traits in breeding programs.
WUE(intr), which is often used as a selection criterion, does not necessarily capture the underlying physiological mechanisms of water use.
WUE(intr), which is often used in breeding programs, is an index that conflates two processes (photosynthesis and stomatal conductances) that are often independently variable.
